## Findings: hobby-router usability, Q1-Q5

Research only, no code. Vendor material (public feature pages, edition tables, the user's own copy of a published tutorial) was used only as a checklist of *which* workflows hobby users expect. No wording, labels, parameter names, layouts, icons or dialog flows were taken; everything below is in our own machining terms. No Autodesk, Fusion or HSMWorks material was read. Codebase facts were read on `upstream/main` (2026-11-20).

Short keys: **VC** = VCarve Desktop/Pro (Aspire noted where only it has a feature), **DP** = DeskProto, **CC** = Carbide Create, **EA** = Easel, **ES** = Estlcam.

**The one fact that matters most:** every hobby tool starts from a **2D drawing or a picture**, and CamCraft today starts from a **3D model**. DXF profiles can be placed (#1862), but `sketch_model::generation_problem` still refuses every 2D toolpath on them ("not generated yet"). Until #1864 / #1867-#1870 land, the most common hobby job cannot be done without first building a solid. That is exactly MisterMaker's complaint in #3038.

### Q1. Typical first jobs: steps and knowledge needed

Steps are counted as user decisions from an empty project to a saved program. "Knowledge" means what the user must already know.

| Job | VC / DP (typical) | CamCraft today | Where we cost more |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1. Sign or plaque cut-out** (outline + holes from a drawing, through a sheet, with tabs) | ~6: sheet size and thickness, Z zero (top), XY zero corner; load drawing; one profile cut (outside for the outline, inside for holes found automatically by nesting level); tabs with defaults sized from the cutter; preview; save with the machine's post. DP walks this as a fixed guided sequence (tutorial, lesson 1A, pp. 28-35). | **Not possible from a drawing** (DXF generation refused). From a STEP/STL of the plate: ~12: import, machine, setup, stock box, WCS stock point, create tool (no wood cutting data), 2D Contour, pick chains, side, heights (top/bottom/through), tabs, generate, simulate, post. | Needs a 3D model; needs heights and WCS vocabulary; no wood feeds; tabs have open defects (#3019 P3: tabs + default lead held at verify). |
| **2. V-carved name** | ~5: sheet, type text in a font, choose a V-bit, one V-carve cut (depth follows the stroke width, optional flat clearing for wide areas), preview. DP needs the text drawn as curves in the file. | **Missing.** No V-carve (#1443); typed text exists as single-stroke placement (`insert_text`, #2679) but its generation waits on #1869, and a constant-depth engrave is not a V-carve. | Whole job absent. |
| **3. Inlay** (pocket in the base + matching plug from one shape) | ~6 in VC Pro / CC / DP Expert: one shape, a V-bit (and an optional clearing end mill), fit allowance (glue gap), plug start depth; produces two cut sets, one mirrored. | **Missing.** | Whole job absent; depends on V-carve. |
| **4. 3D relief** (a) from an STL, (b) from a picture | (a) ~6: load mesh, size and place it in the block, rough + finish, preview, save; DP offers this as a guided sequence (lesson 2A, pp. 45-50). (b) DP: load image, map grey level to height, size, finish (lesson 3A pp. 65-70; lithophane lesson 8, p. 121). CC Pro and Aspire also turn images into height fields. | (a) **Works**: STL import, 3D Pocket rough + 3D Finish, sim, post; ~10 steps with the setup vocabulary. (b) **Missing**: no image-to-height-field source. | (a) more steps, no guided path; (b) absent. |
| **5. Box part: pocket + profile with tabs** (e.g. a tray) | ~7: sheet, drawing, pocket (island detection, ramped entry), profile with tabs, preview, save. | **Works from a 3D model**: `detect_pockets` makes the Pocket, 2D Contour with tabs, leads and ramps; corner relief (dogbones, #2400) shipped. ~12 steps. From a drawing: blocked as in job 1. | Model first; no starter tools/feeds for wood; no saved "my usual cuts". |

Summary: for jobs 4a and 5 CamCraft already does the machining (and does more checking); the gap is the **entry point** (drawing/text/picture instead of a solid) and the **knowledge tax** (heights, WCS, tool and feed setup with no wood data). For jobs 2 and 3 the machining itself is missing.

| Feature (our terms) | Who has it | CamCraft today | Issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2D drawing (DXF) straight to cuts | VC, DP, CC, EA, ES | **partial**: placement shipped (#1862); generation refused | #1452, #1863, #1864, #1867-#1870, #1865 |
| SVG drawing import | VC, CC, EA | **missing** | #1880 |
| Typed text: single-stroke | VC, ES, EA | **partial**: `insert_text` places strokes; generation #1869 | #2679, #1869 |
| Typed text: outline fonts (closed letter shapes for pocket / V-carve / cut-out) | VC, CC, EA, ES | **missing** | none: propose (S4) |
| V-carving (depth from stroke width, flat clearing) | VC, DP (Entry+), CC, EA, ES | **missing** | #1443 |
| V-bit with a flat tip | VC, CC, EA | **missing** (sharp cone only) | #895 |
| Inlay: matched pocket + plug | VC Pro, CC, DP Expert | **missing** | none: propose (S5) |
| Image / heightmap to relief, lithophane | DP (all editions), CC Pro, Aspire | **missing** | none: propose (S6) |

| Wood / MDF / plywood cutting data | VC, CC, EA (material presets) | **missing**: `WorkMaterial` has aluminium, steels, cast iron, brass, plastics; catalog is 29 of 33 aluminium tools | none: propose (S1) |
| Router bit starter library (up/down/compression end mills, V-bits, ball nose, surfacing) | VC, CC, EA | **missing** | none: propose (S2) |
| Sheet setup: thickness, Z zero top or spoilboard, cut-through allowance | all | **partial**: stock box + WCS stock point; through-depth exists in ops but no spoilboard notion | #1557 (closed, through depth); propose (S1/S3) |
| Material preview with removal | all | **have** (stock sim with rest/gouge colours) | wood colours: cosmetic, not proposed |
| Tiling a job larger than the bed | VC | **missing** | not proposed now (P8 later) |
| Collision / holder check | DP Expert (collet) | **have** (fixtures, holder, machine travel) | - |

### Q3. Defaults and presets for a safe first router cut

Proposal (behaviour, our design):

1. **Material choice drives the numbers.** Add router work materials (softwood, hardwood, MDF, plywood, HDPE/acrylic are partly under Plastics) to the cutting table. Each row gives conservative chip load per tooth by cutter diameter (the standard chip-load relation: feed = rpm x flutes x chip load, Haynes pp. 114-116) and a stepdown limit as a fraction of diameter. Start low: the machine's rated rpm range clamps the result, and the suggestion says so.
2. **Starter router library** (one `.camtools` file, inch and metric twins): 1/8" and 1/4" (3 and 6 mm) 2-flute upcut, downcut and compression end mills, 60° and 90° V-bits, a 1/8" ball nose, one surfacing bit. Each carries stated flute length and shank so the existing holder/reach checks work. Recipes come from published handbook practice, not vendor tables.
3. **Sheet job preset**: thickness first, then Z zero = top of sheet (default) or spoilboard. Through cuts default to thickness + a small stated allowance into the spoilboard (e.g. 0.2-0.5 mm), shown as a number, never hidden (#1557 is the lesson). XY zero = front-left corner by default.
4. **Safe heights from the sheet**: clearance and retract default from thickness + the highest fixture; with no fixture modelled, a clamp-height prompt with a conservative default.
5. **Tabs on by default for through-profiles**, sized from the cutter (count by perimeter; height a fraction of thickness), with the existing bridge check still the judge (#2480, #2561).
6. **Machine presets** for the common hobby frames, each naming its controller dialect and its homing/zero habit (many run unhomed, per `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`).
7. **Ramped entry on by default** for pockets and profiles in wood (router bits plunge poorly; ramped entry practice: Overby p. 167).

### Q4. Simplifications we must not copy, and how to stay simple anyway

| Their simplification | Why it breaks our law | Our simple-but-safe version |
|---|---|---|
| A closed shape the cutter does not fit into is **silently skipped** (described as normal in the DP tutorial, lesson 1A, p. 32) | Silent wrong answer: the program "succeeds" with a feature missing | Generate what fits, and **name every skipped shape** in a warning the user must see before post; offer the smaller tool. |
| V-carving clips depth at the material bottom or a max depth without saying so | Wrong shape, silently | Clip only when the user set a max depth; otherwise refuse with the region that would cut through. Flat clearing is an explicit choice. |
| Material presets as fixed feeds regardless of cutter, rpm limit or flutes | Overload, broken bits, fire risk in MDF | Compute from chip load and the machine's rpm range; clamp and say so; label every suggestion as a starting point. |
| Through cuts default to "thickness" with no notion of what is under the sheet | Cuts the bed or leaves a skin depending on sheet tolerance | Explicit spoilboard allowance, shown; refuse a through cut deeper than the stated spoilboard. |
| Tabs placed by count only, no check that the part stays held or the slug is freed safely | Freed parts fly (a known router hazard, Overby p. 167) | Keep the bridge check; extend detection of freed slugs (#1565). Defaults are fine, unchecked defaults are not. |
| Guided sequences that write their own copy of the settings (a second path) | Two sources of truth, undo gaps | The guided first job is a **checklist over the same undoable commands** (and their MCP tools): each step creates or edits the ordinary setup/stock/tool/operation, so the result is a normal project. Same recommendation as #3045 Q3. |
| No verify before save | Silent gouge | Keep verify in the save path; the guided job ends on simulate + verify, not on "save". |
| Vendor-locked output (free tier only posts to one brand) | n/a (business choice) | Every machine preset posts to its own dialect. |

### Q5. Ranked sub-issues (by how many router users each helps)

Existing issues come first because they unblock the most; I do not propose duplicates of them.

**Existing, already filed (recommend keeping at their priority; they are the critical path):** #1864 / #1867 / #1869 (DXF to cuts, the #1 blocker), #1880 (SVG), #1443 (V-carve), #2679 (typed text), #3019 (P3 tabs held at verify), #3038 (WorkBee), #895 (V-bit flat tip).

**Proposed new sub-issues** (each "Part of #3066", `source:agent`, with a Done-means line when filed):

| # | Title (proposed) | P | effort | area | Why this rank |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Cutting data: wood, MDF, plywood and router plastics work materials, chip load by cutter diameter, clamped to the machine's rpm range | P6 | high (changes posted F/S) | `area:post` (no tools area label exists) | Every router user, every job; today the suggestion refuses or speaks aluminium. |
| S2 | Starter router tool library (inch + metric): up/down/compression end mills, 60/90° V-bits, ball nose, surfacing bit, with stated reach | P6 | medium | `area:post` (no tools area label exists) | Every first job needs tools; no posted-code change by itself. |
| S3 | Guided sheet job: thickness, Z zero top or spoilboard, stated through-cut allowance, XY zero, clearance from clamps, as one checklist over the existing undoable commands + MCP tool | P6 | high (sets heights that reach posted code) | `area:2d`, `area:ui`, `area:mcp` | The step where hobby users break bits or beds; removes the heights/WCS knowledge tax. |
| S4 | Typed text as outline-font closed shapes (pocket, V-carve, cut-out), sharing the sketch entity | P6 | max (font outlines, new geometry) | `area:2d` | Signs and names are the most common hobby job; #2679 covers single-stroke only. |
| S5 | Inlay: matched pocket and mirrored plug from one shape, with a stated fit allowance, verified as a pair | P8 | max (needs #1443) | `area:2d` | High demand, but waits on V-carve. |
| S6 | Relief from an image: grey level to a height field (size, depth range, invert, smoothing) as a 3D source for 3D Pocket / 3D Finish; lithophane as a preset | P8 | max (new geometry source) | `area:3d` | Big for DP users; the 3D ops already exist, only the source is new. |
| S7 | Saved cut recipes: store an operation's settings (tool, material, depths, tabs, leads) and apply them to new geometry as an undoable command + MCP tool | P6 | high | `area:2d`, `area:ui`, `area:mcp` | Repeat jobs (signs, boxes); cuts most later steps to one. |
| S8 | Machines: hobby router frames (Shapeoko, X-Carve, Onefinity) machine files with controller dialect and zero habit, after confirming each frame's data | P6 | medium (machine files on existing posts) | `area:post` | Many users; Grbl/grblHAL posts already exist, so mostly data. |
| S9 | Docs: "Your first router part" (sheet cut-out with tabs, a V-carved name once #1443 lands), demo project with a recorded air-cut proof | P7 | low | `area:ui` (no docs area label) | Cheap, and it is how a DP/VC user finds the path. |

Not proposed now (noted for later): 3D tabs for cut-out reliefs, job tiling larger than the bed, photo line engraving, wood-coloured preview.
